'''Richard Conrad''' "'''Con'''" '''Cambie''' (born 1931) is a New Zealand natural products chemist known for his research into bioactive compounds.

Born in 1931 in [[Tauranga]], Cambie was educated at [[Tauranga Boys' College|Tauranga College]].<ref>{{cite news | title=Schools celebrate past times | date=23 May 2013 | work=Bay of Plenty Times}}</ref> He attended [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]], graduating with an [[MSc]] with first-class honours in 1955 and a [[PhD]] in 1958.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university5.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Ca–Cl |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> Appointed to the staff of chemistry department at Auckland in 1958,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cambie |first1=R.C. |last2=Davis |first2=B.R. |title=A century of chemistry at the University of Auckland |url=http://dtlappprd01.its.auckland.ac.nz:1801/webclient/StreamGate?folder_id=0&dvs=1412372706333~446&usePid1=true&usePid2=true |access-date=4 October 2014 |year=1983 |publisher=Percival |location=Auckland |page=43}}</ref> Cambie then studied at the [[University of Oxford]], where he was awarded a [[DPhil]] in 1963.<ref>{{cite book |title=Fungal polyacetylenes |oclc = 155934882}}</ref> He was awarded a [[Doctor of Science|DSc]], on the basis of publications submitted, in 1964.

He returned to the University of Auckland and, following the retirement of [[Bob Briggs (chemist)|Bob Briggs]] in 1969, he was appointed to a professorial chair.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cambie |first1=R.C. |last2=Davis |first2=B.R. |title=A century of chemistry at the University of Auckland |url=http://dtlappprd01.its.auckland.ac.nz:1801/webclient/StreamGate?folder_id=0&dvs=1412372706333~446&usePid1=true&usePid2=true |access-date=4 October 2014 |year=1983 |publisher=Percival |location=Auckland |page=37}}</ref> For 17 years he also served as assistant to the vice-chancellor (student services).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aurfc.co.nz/auckland-university-rugby-football-club/history-of-the-club/ |title=History |publisher=Auckland University Rugby Football Club |access-date=4 October 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006093035/http://www.aurfc.co.nz/auckland-university-rugby-football-club/history-of-the-club/ |archive-date=6 October 2014 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> On his retirement in 1996 Cambie was granted the title of professor emeritus.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.calendar.auckland.ac.nz/personnel/emeriti.html |title=Professores emeriti |publisher=University of Auckland |access-date=4 October 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502040054/http://www.calendar.auckland.ac.nz/personnel/emeriti.html |archive-date=2 May 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1966,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/a-c/ |title=The Academy: A–C |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> and the following year he was awarded the society's [[Hector Medal]], New Zealand's highest science honour at that time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ |title=Hector Medal |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> He is the author or co-author of 430 scientific papers.
